source.title: Poro 34B and the Blessing of Multilinguality
source.authors: Risto Luukkonen; Jonathan Burdge; Elaine Zosa; Aarne Talman; Ville Komulainen; Väinö Hatanpää; Peter Sarlin; Sampo Pyysalo

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Evaluates downstream benchmark performance at successive training checkpoints of a multilingual model, an extension to this setting of the downstream-performance-with-scale question. It does not reproduce a loss-scaling-law experiment.
record.gate_note: The character-level perplexity table compares models with different architectures, training data and token budgets; it is not a controlled scaling sweep or a power-law fit. The paper cites and uses the Chinchilla compute-optimality estimate to motivate training duration but does not test the allocation law. Figure 3 reports FIN-bench results for Poro 34B checkpoints at 10% intervals; checkpoint values are not given in the text.
record.test_reason: A model-release paper. It uses the Chinchilla token estimate (about 700B tokens for 34B) only to choose its training length, deliberately overshooting to 1T tokens, and reports only its own model's performance. The Figure 3 FIN-bench checkpoint curve is one model's trajectory over training. No numbers are given in the text, and there is no fit, no prediction and no link to loss, so it cannot show whether downstream performance improves predictably (V6). The perplexity table compares unrelated models with different data and architectures.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that limited multilingual training (Finnish upsampled to 4 epochs, plus English, code and translation pairs) yields a 34B model that substantially beats prior Finnish models, is competitive for English and code, and is strong at translation. They add that this lifts data limits, 'allowing further scaling' for smaller languages. They draw no conclusion testing any scaling law and note they ran no ablations.
record.recipe_differences: A multilingual 34B model trained for 1T tokens, with FIN-bench checkpoint evaluations; it does not fit parameter-, token- or compute-scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported downstream checkpoint progression is specific to FIN-bench and Poro 34B.

fits_no_version.finding: Poro 34B's FIN-bench score rises over training checkpoints and exceeds FinGPT's best already at 10% (100B tokens), despite Finnish making up about 13% of the data. This is figure only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multilingual augmentation of a data-constrained language lets a larger model surpass monolingual models trained on more target-language tokens.

record.problems: The checkpoint scores in Figure 3 are not stated numerically in the text. There is no controlled scaling sweep or ablation study.

untested.parts: No sweep or power-law fit of held-out loss.
Chinchilla's estimate is used to choose the token budget but is not tested.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Repeated data (4 epochs of Finnish) is used, following Muennighoff et al., but its scaling is not measured.
Only a figure-only checkpoint trajectory for one model on FIN-bench. No predictability test, no fit, and no relation to loss.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' with V6 is overturned. A checkpoint curve from a single run, with values only in a figure, is not a test of downstream predictability. The relation is reclassified as uses_without_test/T4 because the Chinchilla estimate is used as a design input. The authors also remark that perplexity is 'not necessarily predictive of downstream performance', but this is an aside, not a result.

versions.untested_parts: No controlled sweep or power-law fit of held-out loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
No compute-budget allocation sweep or fitted parameter/token scaling trend.
No comparison of architectures at fixed parameter count.
No test of power-law loss scaling in other modalities or the listed training regimes.
Tests checkpoint progression only on FIN-bench for Poro 34B; does not relate downstream performance to pretraining loss or assess other models and tasks.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents or alternative curve shapes.
